title: Warehouse Robot Path
summary: Find the fewest moves for a warehouse robot to reach a pick location around shelving.

stages.title: Fewest moves
stages.requirement:
The warehouse floor is a grid of strings: `"."` is open floor and `"#"` is shelving. The robot
moves one cell up, down, left or right per move and can't leave the grid or enter shelving.
Write `shortest_path(grid, start, goal)`, where positions are `(row, col)`, returning the
fewest moves from `start` to `goal`, or `-1` if it can't get there. If `start == goal`, return
`0`. If either position is a shelf, return `-1`.

```python
grid = [
    "..#.",
    ".##.",
    "....",
]
shortest_path(grid, (0, 0), (0, 3))  # -> 7
```

Grids are up to 500 x 500.

hiddenTests.name: test_large_open_floor
hiddenTests.description: DFS with backtracking, or revisiting cells, is far too slow here.

hints: Every move costs the same, so which graph search finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs?
BFS from `start` with a queue of `(row, col, distance)`. Mark cells visited when you enqueue them, not when you dequeue them.

solution.explanation:
BFS explores cells in order of distance, so the first time it reaches the goal is the
shortest path. Marking cells as seen when they're enqueued means each cell enters the
queue once, which keeps the search linear in the number of cells.
